# Ocufuse

> Ocufuse is an eye fitness and eye health journal web app, with an iPhone app launching October 23, 2026. It offers eye training games, guided eye exercises (including companions for exercises clinicians give for lazy eye, strabismus and convergence insufficiency), comfort routines for eye strain, a practice log, symptom notes, optional eye photos and a Doctor Brief to share with an eye care professional. Ocufuse is not a medical device and does not diagnose or treat any condition. It is free during early access. Web app: https://app.ocufuse.com

## Product
- [Ocufuse: eye exercises, eye training games and eye health journal](https://ocufuse.com/): Eye training games and guided eye exercises for lazy eye, strabismus, amblyopia and eye strain, with a practice log and a Doctor Brief for your eye doctor. Free in your browser, iPhone app coming October 23.
- [For clinicians: reading an Ocufuse Doctor Brief](https://ocufuse.com/clinicians): For ophthalmologists, optometrists, orthoptists and GPs: what an Ocufuse Doctor Brief contains, how patients make it, and its limits.
- [Safety and Intended Use](https://ocufuse.com/safety): What Ocufuse is for, what it is not for, and the eye warning signs that need a doctor straight away.
- [Pricing](https://ocufuse.com/pricing): Ocufuse is free during early access: eye training games, guided eye exercises, a practice log and Doctor Brief in the web app. No card needed to sign up.

## Eye exercises
- [Eye Exercises: What the Research Says and How to Track Them](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/): Do eye exercises improve vision? What eye exercises can and can't do, techniques clinicians prescribe, the CITT and Cochrane evidence, and how to log prescribed exercises.
- [Convergence Insufficiency: Symptoms, Treatment and Exercises](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/convergence-insufficiency): Convergence insufficiency symptoms, how it is diagnosed, and the treatments with the strongest evidence, including the CITT trial and Cochrane review.
- [Pencil Push-Ups and the Brock String Explained](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/pencil-push-ups-brock-string): How pencil push-ups and the Brock string work, why clinicians prescribe them for convergence insufficiency, and what the CITT trial found.
- [The 20-20-20 Rule and Digital Eye Strain: Does It Work?](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/20-20-20-rule): What the 20-20-20 rule is, what digital eye strain is, what a 2022 study found about screen breaks, and AOA screen setup advice.
- [Eye Exercise Myths: Palming, Bates Method and Glasses](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/myths): Can eye exercises replace glasses? What eye care organisations say about palming, the Bates method and eye exercises for dyslexia.
- [Eye Exercise Log: Track Prescribed Eye Exercises](https://ocufuse.com/eye-exercises/exercise-log): What to record when doing prescribed eye exercises at home, a simple log format, and how to bring it to your orthoptist or optometrist.

## Blog
- [Photographing your child's eyes for the eye doctor](https://ocufuse.com/blog/photographing-your-childs-eyes-for-the-eye-doctor): An eye that sometimes turns in or out often behaves perfectly at the appointment. How to capture useful photos and short videos of a child's eyes at home.
- [A red eye: when you can watch it and when to see a doctor](https://ocufuse.com/blog/red-eye-when-to-see-a-doctor): Many red eyes are minor, but some need care the same day. The signs that separate the two, and what to note while you wait for an appointment.
- [Screen eye strain: what actually helps](https://ocufuse.com/blog/screen-eye-strain-what-helps): Tired, dry or blurry eyes after a day at the screen are common. The habits with the best support, what blue light glasses do and don't do, and when to get your eyes checked.
- [Double vision that comes and goes: what to note for your appointment](https://ocufuse.com/blog/double-vision-that-comes-and-goes): If you sometimes see double, a few simple observations make your doctor's job easier. What to check, what to write down, and when double vision is an emergency.
- [A drooping eyelid: what to record and when it is urgent](https://ocufuse.com/blog/drooping-eyelid-what-to-record): When one eyelid sits lower than before, photos taken the same way over time are useful to your doctor. How to take them, what to note, and the signs that cannot wait.
- [What to tell your eye doctor: a checklist for your next appointment](https://ocufuse.com/blog/what-to-tell-your-eye-doctor): Eye appointments are short. A practical checklist of what to bring, what to mention and which questions to ask so nothing gets forgotten.
- [How to keep a dry eye diary your doctor can actually use](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-keep-a-dry-eye-diary): Dry, gritty or watery eyes often depend on the day. A simple diary format that shows the pattern, plus what to bring to your appointment.
- [Eye twitching that won't stop: what to note before you see a doctor](https://ocufuse.com/blog/eye-twitching-that-wont-stop): A twitching eyelid is common and usually settles on its own. What tends to set it off, what to write down, and when it is worth getting checked.
- [Why your eye photos look different from day to day](https://ocufuse.com/blog/why-eye-photos-look-different-day-to-day): Two photos of the same eyes can look surprisingly different. The everyday reasons why, and what they do and don't tell you.
- [Preparing for an eye appointment when symptoms come and go](https://ocufuse.com/blog/preparing-for-an-eye-appointment-when-symptoms-come-and-go): Some eye symptoms disappear right before the appointment. How to keep a simple record so your doctor can see what happens on the other days.
- [How to take consistent eye photos at home](https://ocufuse.com/blog/how-to-take-consistent-eye-photos): Light, distance and angle change how your eyes look in a photo. Six habits that make daily eye photos comparable from one day to the next.

## Help and policies
- [Support and Contact](https://ocufuse.com/support): Answers to common questions about Ocufuse and a contact form. We reply within two working days.
- [Privacy Policy](https://ocufuse.com/privacy): How Ocufuse collects, uses, stores and deletes your personal data, including eye photos and health-related journal entries.
- [Terms of Use](https://ocufuse.com/terms): The terms that apply when you use the Ocufuse app and website.
- [Delete Your Account](https://ocufuse.com/delete-account): How to delete your Ocufuse account and all of your photos and journal entries, and how long it takes.
- [Eye Exercises, Vision Therapy and Eye Photo FAQ](https://ocufuse.com/faq): 44 short, sourced answers: do eye exercises improve vision, what vision therapy is, the 20-20-20 rule, amblyopia, strabismus, convergence insufficiency, and how to photograph your eyes for your doctor.
